title: Implement residency policy orchestrator and KMS consent fanout
author: Sofia Nguyen
release_notes: Adds a residency policy orchestrator microservice and KMS consent fanout; enables staged rollout of region-pin enforcement and audit enrichment. Backwards compatible default policies retained.
description: Context: Customers operating across multiple jurisdictions need a robust, auditable mechanism to enforce data-residency and KMS usage constraints without scattering logic across services. This PR introduces a Residency Policy Orchestrator (RPO) service and a lightweight KMS Consent Fanout to centralize policy evaluation, evidence collection, and audit enrichment in the request path. Motivation: reduce duplication of residency logic, provide a single point for canarying stricter region-pin policies, and attach KMS consent proofs to audit events for downstream compliance tooling. Changes include: 1) New service: rpo/ - a small Go service that evaluates RBACv2-style residency policies, resolves tenant claims, and returns structured decisions plus proof metadata. 2) KMS consent fanout: a non-blocking fanout that records KMS provider selection and consent provenance to the audit enrichment pipeline. 3) Policy format: introduces a compact JSON policy spec (schemas/policy_v1.json) that supports per-tenant overrides, operator-scoped exceptions, and temporal bindings. 4) Middleware hooks: lightweight HTTP/GRPC middleware added to serving-runtime and api-gateway to call RPO and attach decision headers (X-RPO-Decision, X-KMS-Proof). 5) Observability: dashboards and new metrics (rpo.evaluations, rpo.cache_hits, kms.consent_fanout.latency) plus tracing integration. 6) Tests and migration: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration test that exercises the fanout with a mocked KMS consent provider, and a staged rollout plan (feature flag) to migrate traffic gradually. Rollout plan: - Feature flag controlled in config; default off for main traffic. - Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for a single region (us-west-2) for one week, with automated rollback on error-rate or decision-delta alerts. - After canary, enable in all regions and flip audit enrichment fully on. Backward compatibility: when the RPO is unavailable or feature flag off, middleware short-circuits to existing legacy residency checks. Security considerations: RPO signs decision blobs using the service key and includes non-replayable nonce/timestamps to be validated by audit pipeline. KMS fanout only records consent metadata (no secret material). Testing: - Local unit + CI (policy fuzz tests) - Integration harness with a fake KMS provider and audit queue - Load test shim shows <2ms added p95 on decision path at 1000 rps (when RPO cached). Related: ENG-987 (policy designer), SEC-204 (audit enrichment), SUP-442 (customer support ticket requesting per-tenant residency exceptions). Documentation: updated design doc (docs/residency-orchestrator.md) and API notes for middleware.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Please ensure service key rotation is documented and the RPO validates notarized timestamps to avoid replay attacks.
Sofia Nguyen: Added a section to docs/residency-orchestrator.md about key rotation and nonce handling; RPO now includes timestamp+nonce in signed decision blob.
Priya Rao: I'm concerned about fanout backpressure when audit queue is down. Can we make the fanout best-effort and surface a metric?

Sofia Nguyen: Fanout is implemented as non-blocking; writes to audit queue are retried with bounded buffer and we emit kms.consent_fanout.dropped when buffer overflows. Documented behavior in middleware comments.
Marco Alvarez: Tests look good but add a regression test for legacy short-circuit when RPO times out.
Sofia Nguyen: Added integration test rpo_kms_integration_test.go which verifies timeout short-circuit and legacy path behavior.
merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash. Post-merge actions: helm chart bumped, canary feature flag enabled in staging, and CI created a release candidate tag rpo-v0.1.0-rc1.
